paraphrase: Prior absence is beginningless and has an end (of a product before it arises); destruction has a beginning and no end; absolute absence has a counterpositive delimited by a relation for all three times ('there is no pot on the ground'); mutual absence has a counterpositive delimited by identity ('a pot is not cloth').

paraphrase: Ākāśa has sound as its quality and is one, all-pervading and eternal; time is the cause of usages such as 'past', and space of usages such as 'east'; each is one, all-pervading and eternal.

paraphrase: Inferential cognition is produced by consideration (parāmarśa), the cognition of the subject as possessing (the probans) qualified by pervasion — e.g. 'this mountain has smoke pervaded by fire'; pervasion is the rule of co-presence 'wherever there is smoke there is fire'; inference is for oneself or for others, the latter stated with five members.

paraphrase: Each of earth, water, fire and air is eternal as atoms and non-eternal as products, and as product is threefold — body, sense faculty and object: the body of earth is that of beings like us, of water in the world of Varuṇa, of fire in the world of Āditya, of air in the world of Vāyu; the senses are smell (at the tip of the nose), taste (at the tip of the tongue), sight (at the tip of the black of the eye) and touch (spread over the whole body).

paraphrase: Verbal testimony is the statement of a reliable person — one who speaks of things as they are; a sentence is a group of words; a word is what has denotative power (śakti), and that power is the Lord's convention: 'from this word this meaning is to be understood'; expectancy, compatibility and proximity are the causes of understanding a sentence; Vedic statements are all valid because spoken by the Lord, worldly ones only when spoken by a reliable person.
